clue.text: He demands money for a huge platter

definitions.meaning: one who charges a fee or price asks for payment
a large flat dish for serving meat is an old word for a big plate

explanation.surface: Someone bills a customer for an enormous serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: One who charges is a biller, and the same word names a large flat serving dish.

clue.text: Brief agreement

definitions.meaning: short and concise, taking up little room
a pact or contract between parties

explanation.definitionFit: Compact means concise as an adjective and a formal pact as a noun.

clue.text: Director coming in soon to get a firedog

indicators.note: the abbreviation enters the word for soon

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A film director arrives shortly to collect a dog called Fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is one of a pair of metal stands that hold logs in a hearth.

clue.text: Cease to function and leave

definitions.meaning: stop working, as an alarm or a light might
depart

explanation.surface: A machine breaks down and someone walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to stop working and to depart.

clue.text: Passing on gossip is a shopkeeper's job

definitions.meaning: to retail a story is to repeat it to others
selling goods to the public

explanation.surface: Spreading rumours is what a shopkeeper does all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail as a verb means both to recount tales and to sell goods direct to customers.

clue.text: Corporation has reservation getting Dutch currency

parts.note: a guild is an association or corporation of tradesmen
er is the hesitant noise that expresses doubt or reservation

explanation.surface: A company with doubts ends up with Dutch money.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating, so it stands for a reservation or doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilder was the coin and monetary unit of the Netherlands before the euro.

clue.text: Manage to squeeze past

definitions.meaning: cope or survive
to get past someone in a narrow space

explanation.surface: Someone contrives to slip past in a tight corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to survive on little and, literally, to pass an obstacle.

clue.text: Eager to make me paint it

indicators.note: the letters of these words are reworked to make something new

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to get me to paint it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' signals rearranging the letters of ME PAINT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impatient is restlessly keen for something to happen.

clue.text: Putting cover back on Austen novel is a problem

indicators.note: the word for cover is put on backwards, read from right to left

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: Re-jacketing a Jane Austen novel turns out to be tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals reading the word for cover right to left; 'Putting ... on' places it before the novel's title. The surface suggests re-covering a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice or predicament.

clue.text: American white infuriated by left-wing audacity

parts.note: red is the colour of left-wing politics
neck is British slang for cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: A white American is enraged by the cheek of the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infuriated by' is linking; NECK as audacity is British slang, as in having the brass neck to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: A redneck is a derogatory term for a poor white rural American, especially from the South.

clue.text: Claimed to have been a success

definitions.meaning: to make out something is to assert or allege it
to have ... is to have prospered or got on well

explanation.surface: Someone boasted of a past triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both alleged, as in he alleged he was ill, and having prospered.

clue.text: Executed about fifty after being ousted

indicators.note: the word for executed goes around the numeral, so about here means surrounding

parts.note: to top someone is slang for to kill or execute them
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people were put to death after being thrown out of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside TOPPED. 'after being' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler who is overthrown or deposed has been brought down from power.

clue.text: Fanciful description of Tinker Bell?

definitions.meaning: unrealistic, impractical and whimsical
Peter Pan's tiny winged sprite is light as air and a fairy

explanation.surface: A whimsical way to describe Peter Pan's tiny companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unrealistically whimsical, and literally describes an ethereal, light-as-air sprite.

clue.text: Casual worker goes to eastern Greek valley

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: A temporary employee travels to a valley in eastern Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe is a famous gorge in Thessaly in northern Greece.

clue.text: Timely indication of stress

parts.note: a grammatical form that shows time, past or present, which is also an adjective for strained and nervous

explanation.definitionFit: A verb form marks time, and the same word as an adjective means taut or anxious under strain.

clue.text: To give further details is complicated

definitions.meaning: to expand on a point
intricate and detailed

explanation.surface: Explaining more makes things intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to expand on a point; as an adjective, intricate.

clue.text: Not informed that candles are needed

definitions.meaning: kept ignorant of the facts
where it is unlit, so you need a light to see

explanation.surface: Someone unaware of a power cut that demands candles.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept uninformed is a figurative lack of light; literally, unlit rooms need candles.

clue.text: What the conductor does for old citizen soldiers

definitions.meaning: a conductor coaches the orchestra or band in rehearsal
a historic militia company of civilians in London

explanation.surface: A musical director's work is linked to an old militia.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainbands were the citizen militias of 16th–17th century London; split, the word says a conductor coaches musicians.

clue.text: Handy replacement of a garden shrub!

indicators.note: the letters of the words handy and a garden are rearranged, with a set left over

parts.note: the middle three letters of the word handy spell the conjunction that gets swapped out
the middle three letters of the word handy spell the conjunction that gets swapped out

explanation.surface: Something convenient takes the place of a plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement of' says the middle of 'Handy' is swapped for 'a garden' and the whole lot reshuffled: the shrub's letters plus the dropped three equal the two fodder pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a flowering bush with large round heads of blooms.

clue.text: Only a snob wants a topper

definitions.meaning: someone who acts superior and haughty
a tall silk top hat

explanation.surface: Only a social climber would want a tall formal hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a haughty, superior person and, literally, a tall silk headpiece.

clue.text: The wishes of French fathers

parts.note: de is French for of
sires are fathers, especially of horses

explanation.surface: What French fathers want.
explanation.definitionFit: Desires are longings or wants.

clue.text: Understood by Irish leader involved in diplomacy

indicators.note: the opening letter is wrapped up inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is skill in handling people delicately

indicators.note: the leader of the word Irish is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An Irish politician's diplomatic dealings are grasped without words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is implied or understood without being stated.

clue.text: Token for a teller

definitions.meaning: a disc used as a playing piece or substitute coin
one who tallies or counts votes

explanation.surface: A coin for a bank cashier.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter is a gaming disc and also one who counts, as a teller counts votes.

clue.text: Produced yarn, net and leather there

indicators.note: the letters are brought out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A factory turned out yarn, nets and leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced' signals rearranging YARN and NET; 'and' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where hides are turned into leather.

clue.text: Blast! No relish!

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
O, the figure zero, means none or no

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance that there is no pickle left.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with zest and enthusiasm is doing it with keen enjoyment.

clue.text: Model fellow born one of five

parts.note: a man is a fellow
ne, from French, means born, as with a man's original name
a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: A fashion model was born one of quintuplets.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy used to display clothes in a shop window is a dress model.

clue.text: News channels in an Old Asian country

definitions.meaning: the press, radio and television
an ancient kingdom of the Medes, in what is now Iran

explanation.surface: Broadcasters operating in an ancient Asian land.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the plural of medium for news outlets and also the ancient land of the Medes in Persia.

clue.text: No sex maniac released by Yeoman officers

indicators.note: a maniac behaves wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A sex-crazed lunatic is freed by Beefeaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maniac' reworks NO SEX; 'released by' is linking. The Yeomen of the Guard are the British sovereign's ceremonial bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Exons are four junior commanding ranks in the sovereign's ceremonial bodyguard, the Yeomen of the Guard.

clue.text: Rex meets Virginia in rigorous US university

indicators.note: the king and state go inside the word for rigorous

parts.note: hard means severe or rigorous
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king
VA is the US state abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A king and a state are combined within a demanding American college.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard is the Ivy League university in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

clue.text: A job offered to the French missionary

parts.note: a post is a job or position
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone is given a position by the French, as an evangelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Christian evangelists sent out to preach were the twelve disciples.

clue.text: Sets are distributed in mosaic

indicators.note: the letters of sets and are are spread around into a new order

explanation.surface: Pieces are set out to form a picture made of small tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges SETS and ARE; 'in' links to the definition, a tessera being a piece in a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles or cubes from which a mosaic picture is built.

clue.text: "I am not come to —, but to fulfil" (St Matthew's Gospel)

definitions.text: "I am not come to —, but to fulfil" (St Matthew's Gospel)

parts.words: "I am not come to —, but to fulfil" (St Matthew's Gospel)
parts.note: a quotation from the Sermon on the Mount about the law and the prophets, with the missing verb opposed to fulfil

explanation.walkthrough: Matthew 5:17 reads: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb is the opposite of fulfil: to abolish or wreck the law.
